annotation.title_clean: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation: government response
annotation.title_en: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation: government response
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (UK Government)
named_instruments_referenced: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: UK Government's February 2024 response to its AI regulation white paper consultation. It keeps a non-statutory, context-based, regulator-led approach built on five principles, funds regulator capability and a central function, and sets out early thinking on future binding requirements for developers of highly capable general-purpose AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: Retains five cross-sectoral principles applied by existing regulators on a non-statutory basis, kept under review.
Creates central function: cross-economy AI risk register, monitoring and evaluation, steering committee, regulator coordination.
Announces over £100m including £10m to boost regulator AI capabilities and £80m for nine research hubs.
Considers future targeted binding measures for developers of highly capable general-purpose AI using compute and capability thresholds.
Regulators asked to publish AI strategic approach updates by 30 April 2024; AI Safety Institute supports testing.
